title: Endings
human_question: When a life ends, what did it leave behind, and what carries on?
journey: Chathura meets endings and what surrounds them: funerals, almsgivings for the dead, memory, elders reflecting on what they have done.
surface: Grief, remembrance, responsibility and awe, and how communities hold death.
depth: Death is a cognitive process like any other: the last moments of one life condition the first of the next, with nothing passing across. Kamma is intention and its results, not fate. It is ordered by function, by weight, and by time of ripening. The planes of existence and rebirth-linking show what continuity means without a traveller.

arc.opening: Something left behind by someone who is gone. Object 8 is acquired here.
arc.middle: Actions and their results, causes of death, what the living do for the dead, the last moments of a life.
arc.closing: If nothing passes across and yet everything continues, something must connect it all.

lesson.in_simple_terms: A life does not settle everything before it ends: some of what a person did is still unfolding, some never comes due, and what reaches the dying still matters. The texts describe actions as intentions whose results ripen in different ways and at different times, not as fate or punishment, and they say nothing crosses from one life to the next, yet what follows is not a stranger.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ජීවිතයක් අවසන් වන විට සියල්ල විසඳී නොයන බවත්, කර්මය යනු ඉරණමක් හෝ දඬුවමක් නොව චේතනාව සහ විවිධ කාලවල විවිධ ආකාරයෙන් මෝරන එහි ඵල බවත් ග්‍රන්ථ උගන්වයි. එක් ජීවිතයකින් ඊළඟට කිසිවක් රැගෙන නොයන නමුත් හේතු ඵල දාමය නොකැඩී ඉදිරියට යයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma defines kamma as intention (cetanā) and orders its results in several ways: by the job an action does (producing, supporting, obstructing or cutting off), by which ripens first at the end of a life (weighty, near-death, habitual, reserve), and by when it ripens (this life, the next, later, or never). Later actions can strengthen or weaken earlier ones, and some actions simply lapse. Death comes in four ways, and an untimely death gets its opening through ordinary dangers that skilled care can sometimes avert. Dying is itself a short process of the senses and the mind, after which a rebirth-linking consciousness arises at once, with nothing crossing over, in one of many planes, none of them permanent. Recollecting death wisely is taught as a way to live with urgency and less clinging rather than fear.
progression: EPD-0067 What Was Left Behind: a life ends unfinished, and what carries on is a chain of causes, not a traveller.
EPD-0068 The Seventh Day: the living can still share good with the dead, by telling what they did well enough to be rejoiced in.
EPD-0069 What Comes at Dusk: the texts' map holds many unseen kinds of life, and where a life starts is not the whole story.
EPD-0070 The Ledger: results keep different clocks, this life, the next, much later, and some lapse and never come due.
EPD-0071 When the Rain Stops: nothing is exempt from ending, not even worlds, and their end begins in an ordinary field.
EPD-0072 The Opposing Good: no act has the last word; later good can weaken the force of earlier harm.
EPD-0073 The Boundary Walk: harm begins in the mind, and a passing wish differs from a settled wish to take.
EPD-0074 The Night Shift: death comes in four ways, and early death rides on ordinary dangers that care can meet.
EPD-0075 Called to the House: dying is still lived through the senses, and a good friend at the bedside matters.
EPD-0076 As Long As It Takes: the depth of a trained mind shapes what can follow, and the higher worlds hold fewer doors, not more.
EPD-0077 Sitting With It: death remembered wisely brings urgency and lightness rather than fear.
EPD-0078 The Tools: nothing crosses over, yet what follows a life is new and not a stranger.
lesson.builds_on: Group 7 left the body at its end, made partly by past action and marked by decay from the start, and asked what carries on; this group answers with actions that ripen on different clocks and a stream of mind that continues with no one crossing over.
lesson.hands_to_next: If nothing passes across and yet everything continues, what connects it all? The next group follows that thread as conditions: how each thing arises only with the support of others, and so can also come to an end.
